review.brief_reason: Under ordinary real semantics the merging of terms over the common denominator x5 would be valid, but the expressions use gplearn protected division (div(a,b)=a/b if |b|>0.001 else 1). Combining fractions across protected divisions is not semantics-preserving: when |x5|<=0.001, 5*x2/x5 + 4*x4/x5 evaluates to 1+1=2 while (5*x2+4*x4)/x5 evaluates to 1. The same defect affects the merged terms inside sin(...) in three other places (5*x2/x5+4*x4/x5, 5*x2/x5+5*x4/x5, and the large x1/x5+6*x2/x5+6*x4/x5+(...)/x5 term). A concrete counterexample at (x1,x2,x3,x4,x5)=(1,0,1,1,0) gives original ~= 12.633 vs proposed ~= 13.120, a difference of ~0.487. Variable names are unchanged and both expressions remain total under protected semantics, but the protected-division operator structure was materially altered.
review.counterexample: (x1,x2,x3,x4,x5) = (1,0,1,1,0): under gplearn protected div, original first term 5*x2/x5 + 4*x4/x5 = 1+1 = 2, proposed (5*x2+4*x4)/x5 = 1; full evaluation gives original ~= 12.633, proposed ~= 13.120 (difference ~= 0.487).
